findings.title: Fallback locales are not loaded for non-controller translation calls
findings.body: The new fallback mechanism relies on ApplicationController#set_locale calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! to load all fallback locale files. However, I18n.translate still only calls load_locale for config.locale. Any translation performed outside a controller request—mailers, background jobs, rake tasks, console, or an explicit I18n.with_locale—will not have SiteSetting.default_locale or :en translations loaded. The I18n::Backend::Fallbacks backend will try those locales, find no loaded translations, and still raise/return a missing translation even though the fallback should have resolved it. Fallback loading needs to happen in translate/load_locale itself, not only in the controller before_filter.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the dynamic fallback chain
findings.body: The LRU cache key is built only from the key, current locale, and backend id. A cached value may actually have come from a fallback locale, and the fallback chain depends on the runtime value of SiteSetting.default_locale. If an admin changes the site default locale, previously cached fallback translations for a user's locale remain stale until evicted—e.g. a missing French key cached from the old English fallback will keep returning English after the site default switches to German. The cache key should include the fallback chain/default locale, or the cache should be cleared when the default locale changes.

findings.title: No tests for fallback order or fallback loading
findings.body: This PR adds non-trivial behavior: a custom fallback order, inclusion of I18n::Backend::Fallbacks, and lazy loading of fallback locale files. No tests are added to verify that a missing key in a user's locale falls back to SiteSetting.default_locale and then to English, or that fallback locales are actually loaded. This is easy to regress and affects user-visible strings.
